Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

WeGrowHealthR 1.0.1

Corrections

  • The CRPS in wgh_score() and wgh_score_rows() is now the trapezoid-rule integral of the pinball loss over the quantile levels, with the loss taken to fall linearly to zero in the tails. Each quantile is weighted by the spacing of its neighbours. The earlier equal-weight mean underestimated the CRPS on unevenly spaced grids by about 30% for the default conditional reference grid. wgh_condref_compare(), wgh_condref_cv() and the conditional references flow use the corrected score. New tests compare it with the closed form on uneven grids and with forecasts of wrong tail behaviour.
  • wgh_paired_scores() computes its p-value with the centred bootstrap, (1 + #{|d* - mean(d*)| >= |d|}) / (B + 1). The interval remains the main result. A simulation test checks the size and power of the test.
  • wgh_download() accepts the named value returned by tools::md5sum() and ignores case and spaces in md5. When the destination cannot be replaced in one rename, the old file is moved to a backup, the new file is moved in, and the backup is restored if that fails. New tests simulate failed renames and copies. md5 defaults to getOption("WeGrowHealthR.growdat2_md5").

Simulation

  • With monotone = TRUE (default), measured heights are now made non-decreasing by isotonic regression of each child’s values (the closest non-decreasing sequence), instead of sorting them. Values change only where measurement error created a decrease, and no value moves to another visit. monotone = FALSE keeps raw measurement error and is documented as the choice for methods that must cope with negative observed increments.
  • True heights are checked for monotonicity directly. If overrides make a true curve decrease, it is replaced by its running maximum and velocity_true set to 0 where it is flat, with a warning. Before, only the stored velocity was clipped.
  • New tests compare both measurement modes: error mean and SD by age band, BMI distribution, observed velocity and height-for-age band transitions.
  • The bundled datasets and the precomputed vignettes were regenerated.

CRAN preparation

  • Examples that need a suggested modelling package (46 help pages) now run only when that package is installed (@examplesIf), so the package checks cleanly without suggested packages. Tests and vignettes were already conditional. Checked in a library holding only the required packages.
  • DESCRIPTION spells out the SITAR and SHAP acronyms, cites the SITAR and linear quantile mixed model papers with DOIs, and declares Language: en-GB.

Further corrections and tests

  • A wgh_data object now behaves like its data: x$age, x$bmi <- ..., x[rows, ] (returns a wgh_data), x[rows, cols] and nrow(x). Before, x[rows, ] failed, so the README example did not run. See ?wgh_data_access.
  • wgh_zscore() and wgh_reference() return NA for negative ages (for example a date of birth entered after the measurement date). Before, the WHO 2006 table was extrapolated and gave impossible z-scores.
  • New boundary tests: values exactly on a WHO cut-off, missing and out-of-range inputs, sex codes, mutually exclusive categories and the CDC percentile rules.
  • A missing suggested package is now reported with the function that needs it.
  • A test checks the frozen Book 2 cohort on the GitHub release: checksum, identical repeated downloads and rejection of a wrong checksum.
  • README: what the optional packages are needed for, typical computing times by run mode, and the difference between software validation and clinical validation. cran-comments.md lists only observed check results.

Release

  • wgh_download() downloads the frozen Book 2 cohort from the GitHub release by default and verifies its checksum. It regenerates the cohort locally when offline.
  • Repository, website and issue tracker links in DESCRIPTION, the README, CITATION.cff and _pkgdown.yml.
  • The package is cited as software (citation("WeGrowHealthR")). Study papers are cited with wgh_references(). Shorter title for CRAN.
  • GitHub Actions workflows for R CMD check --as-cran on Linux, Windows and macOS with all suggested packages, a weekly and pre-release integration workflow that runs all 14 flows on the three systems, and a pkgdown site.
  • CITATION.cff, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, issue templates and cran-comments.md.
  • README wording on suggested packages and on the research program corrected.

WeGrowHealthR 1.0.0

Simulation

  • wgh_simulate() keeps every child’s measured heights non-decreasing with age (monotone = TRUE, default), so the observed height velocity is never negative. The true growth curves are always increasing and are checked. monotone = FALSE gives raw measurement error. The bundled data were regenerated.

Parallel computing

  • Bootstraps (wgh_rq(), wgh_lqmm(), wgh_sitar_ci(), wgh_scalar_quantiles(), wgh_mediation(), wgh_link_outcome(), wgh_cluster_stability()), the quantile grid of wgh_lqmm() and the cross-validation folds of wgh_benchmark(), wgh_condref_cv() and wgh_condref_compare() run on parallel workers when a plan is set with wgh_parallel().
  • Every task gets its own L’Ecuyer-CMRG random stream, so results are identical sequentially and in parallel, whatever the number of workers. Workers receive only the objects a task uses.
  • wgh_parallel() validates all arguments before changing anything. New wgh_parallel_info(). New vignette parallel-computing.

New tools

  • wgh_false_moves(): share of band changes caused by measurement error.
  • wgh_quantile_forest(): quantile random forests, also available as a benchmark in wgh_condref(forest = TRUE), wgh_condref_cv(forest = TRUE) and predict(type = "forest").
  • wgh_score_rows(), wgh_paired_scores() and wgh_condref_compare(): row-level scores and child-by-child paired comparisons of references with a child-level bootstrap.

Robustness

  • wgh_download() writes the verified file with an atomic rename, checks every file operation and never replaces an existing destination with an unverified file.
  • New validation tests against published WHO and CDC values, the anthro and anthroplus packages, closed-form scores, simulations with a known truth and matrix exponentials of multistate intensities. The integration tier now runs all 14 flows, checks SITAR recovery of known timing and the model selection rule.

Documentation

  • The reproducing-the-program vignette runs and explains all 14 flows.
  • Every precomputed vignette states that its results come from simulated data and gives the run settings.

WeGrowHealthR 0.10.0

Revision after the author’s review and an external code audit.

Names and data

  • All function, data and preset names now use the wgh prefix, for example wgh_data(), wgh_like and wgh_targets.
  • Example data use a site column for the school site.
  • No institution names, place names or other identifying information appear in the package outside the formal citations of the studies.
  • Studies are cited formally everywhere. wgh_references() returns the full citation and DOI of every study a flow reproduces, in the order requested.

Data contract and references

  • wgh_data() computes age at measurement from the date of birth and the date of measurement (dob, date, date_format), fills missing recorded ages from dates, warns when recorded and date-based ages disagree, and accepts ages in years, months or days.
  • CDC 2000 growth charts (cdc_lms) are available in wgh_reference(), wgh_zscore(), wgh_add_zscores() and wgh_classify(system = "cdc"), together with custom LMS tables. wgh_add_zscores(percentiles = TRUE) adds percentiles. The provenance of the WHO and CDC tables is documented.

Plots

  • wgh_plot_growth_chart() draws percentile or SD curves (lines) from the WHO, CDC or a custom reference, with optional bands, labels and several children.
  • Every plot function and plot() method accepts the display options of wgh_plot_options() (titles, labels, font size, legend, palette, point size, line width, transparency, intervals, facets and axis limits).
  • wgh_plot_fan() opens the fan at the baseline measurement, overlays later measurements and the unconditional range, and no longer draws single-point lines. New wgh_condref_centile() and wgh_plot_condref_calibration().
  • New wgh_plot_child_prediction(), wgh_benchmark_intervals() and wgh_benchmark_shap() show and explain individual height predictions.

Robustness

  • Reports record the status of every model (model_status: ok, failed or skipped, with the reason and any warnings), print it and export it.
  • Seeded functions restore the caller’s random number state. Subsampling in the flows takes a seed argument.
  • wgh_config() validates setting names and values.
  • wgh_parallel() gains max_size and restores future.globals.maxSize.
  • wgh_download() writes atomically, verifies checksums and records provenance.
  • wgh_fit_sitar() limits the number of children by run mode (max_children).
  • Every function that uses an optional package checks for it.
  • Every exported function and dataset has examples.

Documentation

  • Vignettes were rewritten to explain code, options, outputs and next steps, and new study vignettes reproduce the tables and figures of each study: trends-malnutrition, trajectories, growth-curves, growth-distributions, phenotypes-states and prediction. The study vignettes are precomputed.
  • The tutorial covers ages from dates, WHO and CDC references and growth chart options.

Tests

  • New tests for dates to age, CDC references, plot options, conditional reference calibration, transition counts, configuration checks, random number state, downloads, model status and legacy options, and an integration tier (WGH_INTEGRATION=true).
